work.problem: The Builder consults Kappa only when a prompt or handoff happens to send it there: no rule requires it before diagnosis, and nothing checks that it happened (Kappa-first, KAN-60 slice 3, read side).

findings.reason: Same class: a written journal rule with no check. Its correction (a check run on every PR, shown failing on fixtures) is the pattern: the Kappa-first rule ships with its check in the same PR.
findings.revalidation: The append-only check still runs in journal.yml on every PR (read at 0175fc2); the new check is a step in the same job and image, so the pattern applies unchanged.

findings.reason: Recurs F-0014: a journal rule (CAPA fields) whose preventive check was planned and never built. Lesson: do not merge the Kappa-first rule as text with the check left for later.

The design record had rules and a reference checker but no gate step that called them. Lesson: the reference retrieve() in harness_reference.py exists and is called by nothing; the new retrieval must be wired into a running workflow, not only tested.

A projection with no test that compared its output with its source cut fields silently. The slice reads journal entries, including the five 2026-11-08 entries in the plain form, so tests compare slice output with the real entries' text in both forms.
findings.revalidation: entry_fields in capa_project.py (merged in #99) parses only the bold-list form; checked against F-0025, which uses plain Rule: lines, so kappa.py adds a plain-form fallback instead of trusting it.

findings.reason: Its lesson: a suite can pass every designed-to-fail case and still miss a branch of the rule. The checker is mutated by hand after its tests pass, and every surviving mutant gets a case.

A metric built on a hand-set field overstated what it measured. The new check proves the record is complete against recomputed Kappa and came first; it does not prove the reasoning is good. The rule's wording and the PR must say exactly that, no more.
The class this rule exists to prevent: a diagnosis from declared state without the history or the live evidence. Prior knowledge would have pointed to F-0034's open preventive action.

Same class: a decision from memory without checking (a trigger GitHub Actions does not have). The rule requires checking history and current evidence before acting; this PR's workflow change uses only the existing pull_request trigger and github context fields.

Same class: a diagnosis from the latest evidence only. Its preventive action (read the streak from the first run) is a special case of what Kappa-first generalizes: read what is already known before diagnosing.
Selected through F-0097, which corrects it. The apply failures themselves are not in this change's scope.
Selected through F-0097. The disabled apply workflow is sovereign-vpc-gcp's and is not touched here.
Selected through F-0089, which restated its cut fields. Dependabot's access to the private CI does not bear on this change.
A boundary named in the docs before its contract existed. The learning handoff is a new boundary, so it gets a versioned schema (kappa_learning.v1), an example and contract tests in the same change.
Same lesson as F-0029: the record's format is written as a contract before anything parses it, so the checker and the Builder agree on one shape.
Agent commits are still made under the owner's GitHub connection. This clone's configured author is Claude, and the commits keep it; no author is set on the command line (F-0096's lesson).
Work Tracking Rules: the work needs a ticket before it starts. KAN-60 carries it (slice 3, read side); the comment was added before this record.
The register's ranking and deadlines are read, not changed. The slice reports severity and status but adds no ranking of its own.

Consumers vendor only AGENTS.md and schemas, not the register. The next increment (the central gates.yml step) must fetch the register at the pinned playbook commit, like the license evaluator; out of scope here.
The sync action's provenance labels are not touched by this change.
Dependabot pull requests are exempt from the learning record: they are the dependency_patch class, with no diagnosis step. The exemption is shown in the run, not silent.
Governance baseline constraints are unrelated to this change.

lessons: Ship the rule and its check in one change, with designed-to-fail cases (F-0014, F-0027, F-0030).
Test the retrieval against real entries in both journal forms, not only the bold-list form (F-0089).
Mutate the checker after its tests pass; a passing suite can still miss a branch (F-0098).
Claim only what the check proves: completeness and order, not reasoning quality (F-0019).
A new boundary gets a versioned contract first (F-0022, F-0029).
uncertainty: Only Playbook pull requests are enforced by this change; the other repositories wait for the central gates.yml step.

The check verifies that the record existed before the first implementation commit, not that its first version was complete; a later update is allowed and only the final version is checked against current Kappa.
The query (rules and fingerprints) is chosen by the agent. Open findings in the component are always required, but a too-narrow query can leave out a closed finding that would have helped.
